Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — expected traffic profile & SLO targets

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this. We're preparing an annual committed capacity contract and wanted Redwood's input on sizing. High-level ask: support an initial commit equivalent to ~50M tokens/day with burst headroom up to ~1.2k tokens/sec over a 10-minute window.

Performance targets we care about: 95th pct latency for user-facing generation at <= 300ms end-to-end, p99 under 700ms. Typical request size today averages 250 tokens (with tails to 2k tokens), and about 40% of requests include function/tool calls. Peak traffic is concentrated in US evening hours (PST).

Can your team map this to an initial Dedicated capacity proposal (GPU slab counts, expected tokens/sec per slab, suggested headroom %) and any assumptions you need? We also need an estimate of monthly committed spend for the baseline and for a +30% burst buffer.

I'll loop in Tom (procurement) once we have numbers.

Thanks,
Asha Rao
Head of ML Platform
NimbusEdge

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — initial capacity math (work-in-progress)

Hannah / Asha — quick WIP note after looking at the provided profile (assumed median request 250 tokens, 95p ~ 900 tokens, peak sustained window target 1.2k tokens/sec). Key assumptions: model = 34B quantized variant with KV cache behavior; average effective tokens/sec per A100-like slab (mixed batching + prefix cache) ~ 1,500 tokens/sec under typical burst-friendly scheduling; tail latencies depend strongly on sequence length.

Roughs:
- Baseline commit (50M tokens/day) -> avg sustained ~ 578 tokens/sec (24h average).
- To meet 95p <= 300ms for interactive requests, we target per-request latency budget equivalent to ~10–14ms per token at the runtime level; with batching and caching that maps to an operational per-slab capacity of ~1,500 tokens/sec keeping 95p in budget for common sequences.
- For the 1.2k tokens/sec 10-minute burst window we recommend 2 dedicated slabs for headroom on top of baseline slabs (baseline slabs = ceil(578 / 1500) = 1 slab; but 1 slab is too tight operationally).

Recommended initial Dedicated footprint (conservative):
- Commit pool: 2 slabs (provides steady-state redundancy and maintenance headroom).
- Burst buffer: +2 slabs for 10-minute concurrency spikes (on-demand or reserved burst).
- Operational headroom target: 40% above steady-state to maintain p95 SLOs during short hot windows and to absorb model variance.

Cost sketch (commercial to refine): baseline 2 slabs reserved => X USD/month; burst capacity when used billed or pre-reserved at a reduced rate. I'll put the detailed token->slab sheet in a spreadsheet.

I'll attach the spreadsheet with per-slab tokens/sec estimates and sensitivity (delta for 20/40/60% headroom).

Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Final: Dedicated footprint, token->slab mapping & next steps

Tom / Asha — attaching a concise PDF SLO mapping and the spreadsheet Ben produced. Summary of agreed recommendations: 

- Token->slab mapping (conservative): 1 slab ~= 1,500 tokens/sec sustained (model: 34B quantized, assumptions in doc).
- Committed baseline: 2 slabs reserved -> covers 50M tokens/day with ~40% operational headroom across expected traffic shapes.
- Burst plan: +2 slabs for 10-minute peaks (recommended pre-warmed reserved burst when predictable; otherwise on-demand with short warm-up).
- Pricing: Marissa will send a 3-tier pricing sketch (baseline, +30% burst pre-reserved, on-demand burst). HubSpot deal id: NE-20270607-01.
- SLA: Redwood p95 target 300ms, p99 700ms for the committed configuration. Credits and remediation are documented in our SLA appendix; for capacity-caused SLO breaches we offer pro-rated service credits after investigation (detailed terms to be included in the contract).

Next steps:
1) Marissa to provide the pricing bands and a draft term sheet (DocuSign link below).
2) Asha to confirm whether NimbusEdge prefers pre-reserved burst or on-demand for seasonal fluctuations.
3) We will hold the recommended slab reservation for 5 business days pending confirmation (to align hardware capacity).

Attachments: slo_mapping_matrix_v1.pdf (PDF, 420 KB), nimbusedge_mip_estimate.xlsx (xlsx, 78 KB)
